claims.text: Low-energy Ar+ irradiation at approximately 500 eV can produce a controlled increase in surface defect density in nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts.
Calibrated ion irradiation can increase surface defects while avoiding significant bulk or morphological damage.
The irradiation-induced defects will include surface vacancies and dislocations.
The irradiation-induced surface defect density can be quantified using high-resolution TEM and STM.
Increasing surface defect density alters the local electronic structure of PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst surfaces.
The defect-induced electronic-structure change shifts the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Shifts in intermediate adsorption energies modulate ethanol-oxidation reaction pathways.
Shifts in intermediate adsorption energies modulate ethanol-oxidation kinetics.
Defect-induced electronic and adsorption changes may mitigate catalyst poisoning.
Mitigation of poisoning can enhance catalyst durability.
Defects may alter selectivity by favoring alternative ethanol-oxidation pathways.
The irradiated catalyst will exhibit a significant shift in ethanol-oxidation onset potential relative to the unirradiated catalyst.
The irradiated catalyst will exhibit a modified Tafel slope relative to the unirradiated catalyst.
The irradiated catalyst may exhibit enhanced durability during extended electrochemical cycling.
Quantified defect density will correlate systematically with changes in electrochemical performance metrics.
The proposed defect-mediated behavior applies in acidic ethanol-oxidation media at room temperature.
The proposed behavior applies only while the introduced defect density remains below the level that causes bulk structural degradation.

contradictions.description: The named PtPdRhRuIrOs system contains six elements, whereas the uncertainty field calls it a seven-metal system.
